voice.speaker: odysseus
voice.caption: Odysseus arms himself and heads alone toward Circe's house despite Eurylochus's protest.

voice.speaker: hermes-as-young-man
voice.caption: Where now, unlucky man, alone through these hills and knowing nothing of the ground? Your friends are penned as pigs in Circe's sties — and you march straight in to join them.

voice.speaker: hermes-as-young-man
voice.caption: Here — take this herb of power and carry it against her drugs. The gods call it moly: black at the root, its flower white as milk. Hard for mortal men to dig, but the gods can do all things.

voice.speaker: hermes-as-young-man
voice.caption: When she strikes you with her wand, draw your sword and rush her as if to kill. And before you go to her bed, make her swear the great oath of the gods that she plots no further harm — lest she strip you naked and unman you.

keys.beat: Odysseus arms himself and heads alone toward Circe's house despite Eurylochus's protest.
Hermes meets him in the form of a young man and explains Circe's trap.
He pulls the black-rooted, white-flowered moly from the earth and gives it to Odysseus.
Hermes instructs him to resist the drug, draw his sword, and force Circe to swear an oath.
